body: To confirm, you are using the exact same version when editing? Not swapping versions?

Correct.  Throughout the day doing work in a single instance of Godot, then switching to iTerm to run 'git diff' and 'git commit', I see these changes crop up sometimes but not every time I run 'git diff'.

Did you save these scenes before switching away from the editor?

Unfortunately we'd need more details to be able to pin down what is going on here

I'm not sure whether I saved - if I was about to commit, then I would have just run a test of the game, so they'd be saved, but if I was double checking what I had accomplished so far I might not have saved when switching away.

It's good to hear that this isn't intended behavior, at least.  If you tell me what kind of details you'd like to know beyond whether the scenes were saved when switching away, I'll be glad to report back next time I catch it.

Would need some details on how to replicate this reliably, or we can't really help, we need to be able to figure out if it is happening (and if we can figure out a fix, we need to be able to figure out it *isn't* happening any more)
Are you able to provide any details on how to replicate this?

I don't have reproduction steps, but we have a project that has seen this happen multiple times across multiple contributors, all using `4.4.1-stable`. It happened again recently, which is when we found this issue and took a deeper look. we haven't been able to reproduce it though, such as by using the UID upgrade tool

I haven't been able to nail down the exact repro but it seems to be happening when switching branches, with the editor open and with the `.tscn` selected in the editor (which ends up losing the UID)

something like:
 1. be on feature branch
 2. have godot open with a scene
 3. push feature, make a PR and merge it to main
 4. switch to the main branch
 5. pull the latest main, which contains that merge commit
 6. run git diff and notice UID is removed from the open scene

**I found a way to reproduce the issue.** Using Godot 4.5.1-stable:

- Create a new project.
- Create a new scene, say `node_2d.tscn`. Save it.
- Attach a script, say `node_2d.gd`. Save the scene again.
- Switch to a terminal, rename the script and uid file, and update the .tscn file to point at the new path:
    ```
    mv node_2d.gd foo.gd
    mv node_2d.gd.uid foo.gd.uid
    sed -i 's#res://node_2d.gd#res://foo.gd#g' node_2d.tscn
    ```
  _Notice that this is exactly what `git pull` would do, if the script was renamed in an incoming commit._
- Switch back to the editor. It asks whether to reload the scene; do so.
- Save the scene.
- The uid is now gone from the file:
    ```
    $ cat node_2d.tscn 
    [gd_scene load_steps=2 format=3 uid="uid://bamx8gv7ycx3l"]
    
    [ext_resource type="Script" path="res://node_2d.gd" id="1_wtcfe"]
    
    [node name="Node2D" type="Node2D"]
    script = ExtResource("1_wtcfe")
    ```

---

**The missing uid is caused by an invalid filesystem cache.** This is where the uid is written:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9c561027fc8753e30ff32152d0dcb9727c2f421b/scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp#L1852-L1861

Indeed, the script whose uid is being removed from the .tres file has a uid of -1 (i.e. `INVALID_ID`), according to `ResourceSaver.get_resource_id_for_path(path, false)`, which I could verify using a tool script. However, `ResourceLoader.get_resource_uid(path)` still returns a valid uid.

It got fixed immediately by calling `EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem().update_file(path)`. After running that, re-saving the scene added the uid back to the .tscn file.

In `.godot/editor/filesystem_cache10`, I can see that the broken scripts have uid -1 since they look like `MyScript.gd::GDScript::-1::...`. The third field is the uid.

---

I hope this shows the way towards fixing this annoying issue!

> Indeed, the script whose uid is being removed from the .tres file has a uid of -1 (i.e. `INVALID_ID`), according to `ResourceSaver.get_resource_id_for_path(path, false)`, which I could verify using a tool script. However, `ResourceLoader.get_resource_uid(path)` still returns a valid uid.
> 
> It got fixed immediately by calling `EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem().update_file(path)`. After running that, re-saving the scene added the uid back to the .tscn file.

It sounds like the script text was removed, but its `.uid` file wasn't. And `ResourceLoader.get_resource_uid(path)` doesn't verify if the script file exists; it directly reads the uid from its `.uid` file. 

Edit:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/b15a13eed39d902fafb14ca0637c5827c80b2bc9/core/io/resource_loader.cpp#L114-L125

That's true.
